calibration.source: Drone Part 1 — 5 sections, 486 words, script reconstructed from takes 1/3/4/5/6
calibration.caveat: measured take lengths include leading/trailing silence and pre-retake stutters, so real speech is slightly faster than 3.11 w/s. Treat ~3.1 w/s as the working voiceover rate until a cleaner measurement contradicts it.
calibration.text_rates_uncalibrated: text_lead / text_per_word / text_min are conventions, not measurements. Nothing has been recorded to fit them.
calibration.hold_default_is_null_on_purpose: a wordless beat with no explicit duration has no honest length. Never invent one silently — clock.py flags it and asks.

rates.notes: refit with `clock.py swap clock.json measured.json --calibrate --write` after a recording; the fit lands in `speed`, so rebase it into w0/ks/pauses when it settles.

beats.name: hook
beats.note: The creator's own call: open on the music. The four bars play on piano with no voice, over the engraved score, so the viewer hears the tune before any letters appear.
beats.narration: That's the opening of the Minuet in G, from Anna Magdalena Bach's notebook. Here it is in C, written as a single line of text.

beats.name: the header
beats.narration: The lines at the top set the rules. M is the meter, three beats in every bar. L is the default length, so a plain letter lasts one beat. And K is the key, C, which means no sharps or flats.

beats.name: pitch
beats.narration: Each letter is a note. A capital C is middle C, and a lowercase c is the C one octave higher.

beats.name: length
beats.narration: A slash cuts a note in half. So C slash is an eighth note, half a beat, and two of them fill the space of one plain C.

beats.name: the bars
beats.note: Slow and even: one bar at a time, the bar lit up red in the score and in the text at the same moment, everything else gray.
beats.narration: Bar one is G for one beat, then C, D, E, F as four quick eighth notes. One beat, plus four halves, makes three.

beats.name: the bars
beats.note: Slow and even: one bar at a time, the bar lit up red in the score and in the text at the same moment, everything else gray.
beats.narration: Bar two is G, C, C. Three plain letters, three beats.

beats.name: the bars
beats.note: Slow and even: one bar at a time, the bar lit up red in the score and in the text at the same moment, everything else gray.
beats.narration: Bar three is the same shape as bar one, a step higher: A, then F, G, A, B.

beats.name: the bars
beats.note: Slow and even: one bar at a time, the bar lit up red in the score and in the text at the same moment, everything else gray.
beats.narration: And bar four jumps up to the high c, then back down to C, C.

beats.name: the check
beats.narration: Every bar should add up to three. If one doesn't, then a note is missing, or a bar line is in the wrong place.

beats.name: payoff
beats.note: Let the music run clean at the end, no voice over it.
beats.narration: That's the whole idea. Four bars of music, in about forty characters. Here it is again.
